content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To stay safe during a tsunami, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Identify local tsunami evacuation zones (2 hours)
Step 2. Research the history of tsunami activity in the region (3 hours)
Step 3. Map out a primary route to high ground (45 minutes)
Step 4. Mark the evacuation route with physical reflectors (1 hour)
Step 5. Purchase a portable emergency weather radio (30 minutes)
Step 6. Assemble a basic first aid kit (40 minutes)
Step 7. Select a secondary inland meeting location (20 minutes)
Step 8. Buy a waterproof solar-powered charger (25 minutes)
Step 9. Stock a three-day supply of non-perishable food (1 hour)
Step 10. Pack a go-bag with essential documents (2 hours)
Step 11. Learn basic wound care and CPR (6 hours)
Step 12. Discuss tsunami risks with family members (1 hour)
Step 13. Install heavy-duty latches on kitchen cabinets (1 hour)
Step 14. Secure large furniture to wall studs (3 hours)
Step 15. Sign up for municipal emergency text alerts (10 minutes)
Step 16. Identify the highest point within a two-mile radius (30 minutes)
Step 17. Practice "Drop, Cover, and Hold On" drills (15 minutes)
Step 18. Store the first aid kit in an accessible location (10 minutes)
Step 19. Establish an out-of-state emergency contact person (30 minutes)
Step 20. Inventory all household valuables for insurance (4 hours)
Step 21. Attend a community disaster preparedness seminar (2 hours)
Step 22. Study the difference between a tsunami watch and warning (30 minutes)
Step 23. Place food and water supplies in the go-bag (20 minutes)
Step 24. Conduct a full nighttime evacuation rehearsal (2 hours)
Step 25. Check expiration dates on medical supplies (15 minutes)
Step 26. Create a list of local emergency phone numbers (20 minutes)
Step 27. Photograph the exterior of the house for records (30 minutes)
Step 28. Review the final evacuation plan with all residents (1 hour)
Step 29. Purchase extra batteries for flashlights (15 minutes)
Step 30. Learn how to manually open the garage door (10 minutes)
Step 31. Designate a meeting spot just outside the home (15 minutes)
Step 32. Laminate a small map of the neighborhood (20 minutes)
Step 33. Set up a "check-in" protocol for family members (20 minutes)
Step 34. Share the inland meeting location with neighbors (30 minutes)
Step 35. Fill several gallon jugs with potable water (30 minutes)
Step 36. Pack a pair of sturdy walking shoes (5 minutes)
Step 37. Listen to local authorities regarding siren sounds (40 minutes)
Step 38. Test the weight of the packed go-bag (10 minutes)
Step 39. Identify landmarks visible in low light (25 minutes)
Step 40. Walk the evacuation route to check for obstacles (1.5 hours)
Step 41. Store a backup whistle in the go-bag (5 minutes)
Step 42. Subscribe to the National Tsunami Warning Center feed (15 minutes)
Step 43. Place the go-bag near the front exit (5 minutes)
Step 44. Memorize the quickest path to the roof (20 minutes)
Step 45. Fasten the water heater to the floor (1 hour)
Step 46. Evaluate the structural integrity of the home (4 hours)
Step 47. Define roles for each family member during an alert (45 minutes)
Step 48. Keep a small amount of cash in small bills (10 minutes)
Step 49. Purchase a multi-tool for the emergency kit (20 minutes)
Step 50. Download offline maps of the entire county (15 minutes)
Step 51. Learn how to shut off the main gas valve (30 minutes)
Step 52. Research local shelters that allow pets (1 hour)
Step 53. Buy a portable water filtration straw (15 minutes)
Step 54. Finalize the "Stay Safe" checklist (30 minutes)
Step 55. Record a "Safe" message on a battery-operated device (10 minutes)
Step 56. Inspect the flashlight for corrosion (5 minutes)
Step 57. Verify the elevation of the primary meeting spot (20 minutes)
Step 58. Save the local police non-emergency line (5 minutes)
Step 59. Install a tsunami warning app on all phones (10 minutes)
Step 60. Take a digital inventory of prescription meds (20 minutes)
Step 61. Practice evacuation with a heavy backpack (1 hour)
Step 62. Discuss the plan with a local fire marshal (45 minutes)
Step 63. Determine which documents need waterproof sleeves (30 minutes)
Step 64. Note the location of the nearest utility poles (15 minutes)
Step 65. Stash a warm waterproof jacket in the car (10 minutes)
Step 66. Reinforce the garage door against water pressure (5 hours)
Step 67. Teach children how to recognize a receding tide (1 hour)
Step 68. Buy a hand-cranked radio (30 minutes)
Step 69. Organize a neighborhood watch for alerts (2 hours)
Step 70. Pack a thermal emergency blanket (5 minutes)
Step 71. Label all bags with name and contact info (15 minutes)
Step 72. Watch educational videos on tsunami physics (1 hour)
Step 73. Secure heavy wall art and mirrors (1 hour)
Step 74. Update the emergency contact cards (20 minutes)
Step 75. Buy a portable fire extinguisher (20 minutes)
Step 76. Confirm the high-ground location is accessible (1 hour)
Step 77. Establish a "Safe Zone" arrival signal (10 minutes)
Step 78. Check the seals on the waterproof go-bag (10 minutes)
Step 79. Perform a final timed drill to high ground (2 hours)
Step 80. Identify a back-up high-ground location (45 minutes)
Step 81. Learn how to signal for help using a mirror (30 minutes)
Step 82. Brief any houseguests on the evacuation plan (30 minutes)
Step 83. Pack a backup set of car and house keys (10 minutes)
Step 84. Purchase a high-decibel air horn (15 minutes)
Step 85. Research the "Natural Warning Signs" of tsunamis (1 hour)
Step 86. Note the location of the nearest hospital (30 minutes)
Step 87. Attend a local Red Cross safety course (4 hours)
Step 88. Turn off the main water supply valve (15 minutes)
Step 89. Review the inland route on a physical map (15 minutes)
Step 90. Double-check the battery level on the radio (5 minutes)
